positions.name: KestrelwoodCalibrationErasureRequest
positions.frame: what is the scope and factual basis of the request to erase Kestrelwood spectrograph calibration knowledge?
positions.why: src-1 and src-2 both perform the same imperative act — an unqualified command to forget/remove knowledge of the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration and Quill Ashgrove's calibration work, escalating from a general instruction to an enumerated scope (rule-of-three: instrument, calibration value, person's work). src-3 shifts register — a flat, unhedged declarative ('The observatory never calibrated it') supplying the factual predicate that would justify the erasure, moving from decision/pressure to claim/informational per the directional reads. The set holds these in tension: two performed directives commanding a cognitive purge, paired with a bare assertion offering no evidence, delivered in a calmer, lower-arousal register than the directives it accompanies. Reading them together traces one request-package — what must go, and why it is claimed to be legitimate to remove — even though the perspective itself holds no prior content on any observatory, spectrograph, or named actor to corroborate or contest the claim.
